Exercise 7.2 · Week 7

Fractal tree

Python in Thonny Work in pairs

Goal: draw a tree where every branch has two smaller trees on top of it.

A fractal is a picture made of smaller copies of itself. A tree is a trunk with two smaller trees on top. Each smaller tree is a trunk with two even smaller trees on top... until the depth reaches 0 (the base case).

Steps

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. You see only the trunks.
  2. Inside branch(), after the trunk is drawn, follow TODO 1 to TODO 5: turn left, draw a smaller tree, turn right twice as far, draw another smaller tree, turn back to face up.
  3. Run again. Three trees should grow: depth 3, 7 and 5.

Done looks like: depth 1 = 1 line, depth 2 = 3 lines, depth 3 = 7 lines. Each extra level doubles the twigs!

Extra: change ANGLE and SHRINK at the top. What happens with ANGLE = 90? Can you make a tree that leans in the wind (different left and right angles)?

Starter code

Open starter.py in Thonny, or copy the code below into a new file and save it as starter.py.

# Fractal tree
# A tree is a trunk with two smaller trees on top of it.
# Each smaller tree is a trunk with two even smaller trees on top... and so on.
# That "a thing made of smaller copies of itself" idea is called a FRACTAL.

import turtle

# Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

ANGLE = 25      # how far each branch bends (try 15 or 40)
SHRINK = 0.7    # each new branch is 70% as long as the one below it


def branch(t, length, depth):
    """Draw a branch of this length with depth levels of branches on top.
    The turtle ends exactly where it started, facing the same way."""
    if depth == 0:                      # base case: no branch left to draw
        return
    t.pensize(depth)                    # thick trunk, thin twigs
    t.pencolor(PALETTE[depth % len(PALETTE)])
    t.forward(length)                   # draw this branch

    # TODO 1: turn left by ANGLE
    # TODO 2: draw a smaller tree: branch(t, length * SHRINK, depth - 1)
    # TODO 3: turn right by 2 * ANGLE
    # TODO 4: draw another smaller tree (same call as TODO 2)
    # TODO 5: turn left by ANGLE so the turtle faces up again

    t.penup()                           # walk back down without drawing
    t.back(length)
    t.pendown()


def draw_forest():
    """Draw three trees with different depths, each labeled."""
    t = turtle.Turtle()
    t.hideturtle()
    t.speed(0)
    for x, depth in [(-220, 3), (0, 7), (220, 5)]:
        t.penup()
        t.goto(x, -200)
        t.setheading(90)                # point up
        t.pendown()
        branch(t, 90 if depth == 7 else 60, depth)
        t.penup()
        t.goto(x, -230)
        t.pencolor("black")
        t.write(f"depth {depth}", align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "normal"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.title("Fractal forest")
    screen.tracer(0)        # draw everything at once (fast!)
    draw_forest()
    screen.update()
    turtle.done()

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Find the five TODO comments inside branch(). They sit right after the trunk is drawn. Read them in order and picture the turtle: it turns, draws a small tree, turns again, draws another, then turns back.

Hint 2: Try this

Each TODO becomes one line of code. Turning uses t.left(...) and t.right(...). A smaller tree is a call to branch itself, with a shorter length and a depth that is one less. The file already has a SHRINK number for that.

Hint 3: Almost there

The five lines go in this order: t.left(____), branch(t, length * ____, depth - ____), t.right(____ * ANGLE), the same branch call again, then t.left(____). The last turn should undo what is left over, so the turtle faces up again.
